source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"A surgical mask provides a tighter face seal than an N95 and is preferred for inhalation protection from airborne TB.","B":"A fit-tested N95 is a tight-fitting respirator designed to filter airborne particles; a surgical mask does not provide the same fitted respiratory protection.","C":"An N95 and a surgical mask provide equivalent filtration and fit when both are worn correctly.","D":"An N95 is intended for splash protection but does not filter small airborne particles."}}
source_row.rationale: NIOSH-approved N95 filtering facepiece respirators are designed to filter airborne particles and must fit the wearer's face adequately as part of a respiratory-protection program. Surgical masks are loose-fitting source-control/barrier devices and do not provide the same fitted respiratory protection.
source_row.source_detail: Respirators versus facemasks: N95 filtering facepiece respirators require an adequate seal and provide fitted particulate respiratory protection.
